investigator.note: I prioritised extreme rainfall and flooding due to multiple heavy daily precipitation events (reaching up to 53 mm in 2024) and regional GDACS flood alerts, alongside minor satellite-detected urban or industrial fire occurrences. For flood readiness, I evaluated low-lying terrain exposure, land-cover changes, and walking access to high-rise flood refuges, discovering 38 flood-prone blocks containing 6 educational facilities and over 3,700 residents without a nearby tall building refuge. To assess emergency response and animal safety during disasters, I also evaluated walking access to major hospitals and veterinary facilities across the district.

report.summary: Podilskyi district faces risk from extreme rainfall and flooding, with 38 low-lying blocks housing 16858 residents and 53 mm of single-day rainfall recorded in 2024. Readiness is limited by 10 flood-prone blocks where 3774 residents lack a tall building refuge within 300 m walk, alongside long walking distances to major hospital care. Priority action should focus on establishing flood refuge access and drainage in vulnerable blocks around хутір Софіївка and Varshavskyi Masyv.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Extreme rainfall reached 53 mm in a single day in 2024, and 43.7% of blocks (38 out of 87) are low-lying terrain hosting 16858 residents.

matrix.finding: While 90.5% of residents live within 500 m of a tall building flood refuge, 10 flood-prone blocks housing 3774 residents have no tall building refuge within 300 m walk.

Only 2.3% of residents are within 500 m walking distance of a major hospital in the loaded area, with median walking distance to a major hospital being 2177 m and reaching 5246 m in Varshavskyi Masyv. No fire station is mapped within the 3 km loaded area.
There is 1 hospital, 7 clinics, 2 underground metro stations, 2 underground parking facilities, and 7 designated shelters mapped within the area.
Only 9.8% of residents have walking access to a veterinary facility within 500 m, with median walking distance being 1525 m.
No official emergency evacuation protocol or shelter capacity data for pets or stray animals is recorded in the available dataset.
8 veterinary facilities and 1 animal shelter (ДворНяшкам Дім) are located in the district.

Built-up land cover increased from 65.6% in 2016 to 69.7% in 2025, while tree cover slightly increased from 26.4% to 28.0% and grass cover declined from 0.7% to 0.1%. No protected area blocks are present.

Specific impacts of urban runoff on local water bodies (Blakytne, Куренівське кар'єрне озеро (Пінгвін), Неструїха, Озеро Сирець) during extreme rainfall events are not directly measured in the datasets.
Post-flood ecological restoration tracking is not available in the provided datasets.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Multiple extreme daily rainfall events were recorded (53 mm in 2024, 52 mm in 2003, 40 mm in 2012), driving localized inundation risk across 38 flood-prone blocks.

matrix.finding: 7 underpass segments exist in the district which may be susceptible to water accumulation during heavy rainfall.
3774 residents in 10 flood-prone blocks lack vertical refuge options within 300 m walking distance during flash cloudbursts.
98.3% of residents live within 1000 m of a tall building refuge across the general district area.
No data is available regarding stormwater warning systems or pet care readiness for severe storm events.
Worst-served blocks for veterinary access require walking up to 2743 m (хутір Софіївка) or 2683 m (Квітництво-2) during extreme weather.
No post-storm animal rescue or rehabilitation metrics are recorded.
Water surface area remains at 0.1% in 2025 while tree canopy covers 28.0% of the district area.
Data on soil absorption rates and stormwater retention basin efficiency during extreme rain is missing.
No measurements exist for post-rainfall runoff clearing or natural buffer recovery.

recommendations.why: 3774 residents across 10 flood-prone blocks have no tall building refuge within 300 m walk, with maximum walking distance to refuge reaching 1481 m in хутір Софіївка.
